#7 @user_118: I also made the same settings, but it doesn’t work. To “really” get the phone microphone to work, First, set the “Microphone for calls” to “Hearing Aid Microphone.” Then, when a call starts and a notification appears in the top pop-up asking “Do you want to switch to the phone microphone?”, you must press the “YES” button for the phone microphone to function properly.

#8 @user_118: I always use Samsung’s default phone app. However, surprisingly, the error I mentioned only appears in the Samsung phone app. The symptoms do not appear in Kakao Phone or LINE Phone.

#9 @user_118: I am also using a Galaxy Z Fold 7 running One UI 8.5. However, just as I mentioned, only the hearing aid microphone works. After researching for a few days, I found a way to use the phone’s microphone. Go to Bluetooth Settings - Hearing Aid Settings - ‘Microphone for calls’ - ‘Hearing Aid Microphone’. Set it up this way first. Then, when a call starts, a pop-up notification appears at the top as follows: “Would you like to switch to the phone microphone?” If you press “YES,” the phone microphone “really” works. The hearing aid microphone does not work. However, this is a temporary solution. I wish the microphone could work as configured in the settings menu.

#11 @user_118: Yes, I set it up exactly the same way. However, it does not work as configured. No matter what I set, only the hearing aid microphone works. Also, I do not have the “Device Type” menu. I am certain my firmware is One UI 8.5. The “Device Type” menu was only visible in One UI 9.0.

[房间里 user_112 的对照与判断]

#10 @user_112: My settings for The Galaxy A36 5G, BT 5.4, Android 16, One UI 8.5 Hearing Aids On (out of charger) Tap Settings Tap Connections Tap Bluetooth Tap Settings (gear symbol) for Hearing Aids Tap Default Settings for Calls Select “Phone Microphone” Select Off for “Get notifications to Change…” Select “Done” Phone now displays after step 4 Default microphone for calls: ”Phone microphone” The phone stays in this mode. On calls, the phone mic is used by default, and the audio is streamed to the hearing aids. No switching is required. Edit: I think new to One UI 8.5, at the bottom of the hearing aid settings page there is now a selection for “Hearing aid type” Mine is in the “LE Audio” mode vs a selectable “ASHA” type.

#12 @user_112: You can check the One UI version by: Settings>About Phone>Software Information What you are describing is similar to how my phone was performing prior to the latest update(s) I am now running Android 16, One UI 8.5

#13 @user_112: I see from your original post you have two top tier Samsung phones. It seems to me that both should work, yet neither one does, right? Oticon lists the Intent as fully “compatible” with your phones, If neither works, perhaps it’s the hearing aids themselves, or the app. Maybe you should call or email Oticon support for an opinion. You might also consider starting a new thread with “Oticon” in the title to catch the attention of other Oticon users or retitle this thread.
draft:
Worth saying that you've actually finished the diagnosis here, even though it doesn't feel like it. Two different top tier Samsungs, same One UI, Jay's exact path, and it still won't hold. That rules out the phone side about as cleanly as anyone could. You're not stuck because you missed a setting, you're stuck because there isn't one.

Jay's instinct in #13 is the right one. Here's the shape of it from the build side, so you can stop testing combinations.

Under LE Audio a call isn't one stream, it's a configuration the phone and the aids agree on when the call connects. For the phone to give you downlink into the aids while taking your voice from the phone mic, the aids have to advertise that asymmetric configuration as available. If the Intent firmware doesn't offer it, no phone side setting can conjure it, and the popup you found is the phone dropping to a different configuration at call setup because the one you asked for wasn't on the list.

So the thing worth asking Oticon, in these words, is whether Intent advertises a conversational configuration with the hearing aid microphones inactive. Support will bounce a vague question, but that one has a yes or no answer and it either ends this or turns it into a firmware item. Either way you stop chasing menus.

For what it's worth, a Starkey user on a Pixel 10 Pro ran echo tests and landed in the same place, where selecting the aids as output pulled the uplink onto the aid mics whatever the mic preference said. Three brands and two phone makers now, which is not what a Samsung bug looks like.

If the answer comes back no, your two options until firmware moves are the YES tap every call, or switching to ASHA for calls that matter, since ASHA carries no microphone and hands your voice to the phone by force. Neither is nice. I'd want to know which one I was living with rather than keep testing.
